jokes:
When we got the rental car they told us we were not allowed to offroad. To be fair, we never had a choice since half this country is offroad (the roads were so bad that it was offroading). So when the rental says: No offroad, we said 'Yes no offroad' (but we drove offroad a lot)
I think we ate Khinkali every day
GAMARJOBA and MADLOBA were the only words we knew and spoke (nobody spoke english in this country)
From sketchy hotels to rude taxi drivers trying to scam us we made it

items.title: Mountain Sound
items.why: The Kazbegi stretch is the heart of these photos: golden larches over the rushing river, mist hanging in the valley and a lone horse grazing on the slope, and this song is literally about running through the woods into the mountains. Its stomping gang vocals match the bright, wide-open shots like the Georgian flag at the Gudauri viewpoint.
items.structure: Short intro carries the title over Tbilisi at night and the gold-lit Trinity cathedral; the shout-along choruses drive the mountain and monastery run; the last big chorus goes over the Kazbegi autumn hikes and the song ends on a clean final hit.
items.fit: whole song (~3:30); pick the best ~100 photos and hold the landscapes
items.lyric_hooks: 'Hold your horses now' as a handwritten arrow to the grazing horse in Kazbegi; 'deep into the mountain sound' over the misty valley.

items.title: The Cave
items.why: A lot of the highlights are underground or carved into rock: the stalactites in Prometheus cave, the honeycombed Vardzia cliff, the rock city near Gori and the cave clips. The song starts quiet and builds into a galloping banjo stomp, the same arc as a trip that goes from hushed church interiors to big mountain hikes.
items.structure: Quiet voice-and-guitar opening for the title and Tbilisi; kick drum and banjo come in for the mountain road; the full-band final chorus is the Vardzia cliff reveal, and the song lands on a last strum.
items.lyric_hooks: 'So come out of your cave walking on your hands' as a speech bubble on the clip of the friend standing in the rock-cut cave mouth.

items.title: Wake Up
items.why: The church shots (Sameba glowing gold against the black sky, Gergeti, the candlelit interior with headscarved worshippers) call for a choir, and the wordless 'whoa-oh' chant works as one. The line about turning the summer into dust fits an October trip full of yellow larches and dry autumn hills.
items.structure: Guitar swell and chant intro under the title card; verses and chants over Tbilisi and Kazbegi; the switch into the fast, stomping coda is the road-trip reveal (the driving shot, Kutaisi, Tskaltubo, Batumi), and the coda ends the song.
items.lyric_hooks: 'Before they turn the summer into dust' handwritten over the golden larch hike by the river.

items.title: Chicago
items.why: The driving shot, 8,677 km and a route that zigzags across the whole country are this song's story: a road trip in a van with your friends. Its long string-and-horn passages leave room to hold the big views, like the Borjomi forest gorge and the green ridge with the giant sword.
items.structure: Strings and piano open for the title; the repeating 'all things go' choruses are ideal for steady one-photo-per-bar runs; the layered choir finale goes over Sword mountain and the last day.
items.fit: whole song (~6:00, ~180 photos), the closest to the length guide without a cut
items.lyric_hooks: 'Drove to Chicago' with 'Chicago' crossed out and 'Kazbegi' scribbled in over the driving shot; 'we slept in parking lots — I don't mind' over the rental car.

items.title: Let It Happen
items.why: The Tskaltubo urbex run (peeling colonnades at Stalin's sanatorium, the spiralling stairwells, the overgrown railway station) and the dark observatory domes need something hypnotic and a little strange. At almost eight minutes it is the only pick that can carry nearly all 228 photos at one per bar with no cut.
items.structure: The groove intro carries the title over Tbilisi at night; the skipping-CD stutter in the middle is the drop into the abandoned sanatorium; the strings and vocoder section is the big reveal (Vardzia, Sword mountain), and the outro rides home to the end card.
items.fit: whole song (~7:45, nearly all photos), or one cut to about 5:00 between two identical groove passages
items.lyric_hooks: 'Let it happen' handwritten as the friend peers down the Tskaltubo stairwell; the stutter can 'stick' on the Stalin statue in Gori.

items.title: Mykonos
items.why: The ancient stone places (the rock-cut town near Gori, Vardzia's cliff caves, the monastery arches framing the valley) suit Fleet Foxes' stacked, church-like harmonies. Its 'vision of a gentle coast' line gives the Batumi day its own moment.
items.structure: Finger-picked opening for the title; it builds into the harmony chorus; the big 'brother, you don't need to turn me away' section is the reveal, and the coda gives a natural ending.
items.lyric_hooks: 'I was waiting down at the ancient gate' over the Vardzia and rock-city doorways; 'Mykonos' crossed out to 'Batumi' on the gentle-coast line.

items.title: Levels
items.why: The food and city shots have a cheeky 'top G' energy that suits a festival drop: the bubbling khachapuri, the tower of mtsvadi skewers, the drinking horn at the Dry Bridge market, the Mafia barbershop. Its repeated build-ups also work as an altitude gag as the trip climbs from Tbilisi to Gudauri and Gergeti.
items.structure: The synth-riff intro carries the title; the Etta James 'good feeling' vocal sets up each drop; the first drop hits the Kazbegi mountains, the last one Sword mountain, and the song ends fast.
items.fit: radio edit (~3:20, ~95 photos) for a punchy short cut, or the longer original mix for more photos
items.lyric_hooks: 'Oh, sometimes I get a good feeling' next to the khachapuri ('amai dit eten was crazy goed'); an altimeter counting up on every build.

items.title: Nine Million Bicycles
items.why: Katie Melua was born in Kutaisi, one of this trip's stops, which gives the film a real Georgian link. Its 'that's a fact' counting lines suit the trip stats, and 'twelve billion light years from the edge' was made for the Abastumani observatory telescope shots.
items.structure: Gentle opening for the title; each verse is a 'fact', so use them as chapters (Tbilisi, the mountains, the observatory); the soft last chorus ends on the final photo and the stats card.
items.fit: whole song (~3:15, ~90 photos with longer holds), best for a shorter highlights cut
items.lyric_hooks: 'There are nine million bicycles in Beijing, that's a fact' rewritten as '8,677 km through Georgia, that's a fact' with a count-up; 'twelve billion light years from the edge, that's a guess' over the Abastumani telescope.
